entries.name: Anakiwa

facts.claim: Anakiwa is a settlement in Grove Arm at the head of Queen Charlotte Sound, at the Anakiwa end of the 73.5 km Queen Charlotte Track.
The Queen Charlotte Track stretches 73.5 km from Meretoto/Ship Cove to Anakiwa.
At the track end OSM maps an information shelter, toilets, car parks and a public pier (the wharf).
Anakiwa is about 26 km from Picton or 17 km from Havelock by Queen Charlotte Drive (user guide, not an official source).

entries.ticketUrl_note: No single steward for the bay or settlement; QCTrack (https://www.qctrack.co.nz/, official Queen Charlotte Track site, title verified) belongs to the existing Queen Charlotte Track spot (marlborough-sounds-1), not Anakiwa. Leave out.

coordinates_check.source: OSM: 'Queen Charlotte Track Anakiwa' information node (-41.26399,173.92059), car park way (-41.26411,173.92043) and pier (-41.2648,173.92016) at the track end; the Wikipedia point is the settlement ~650 m west
coordinates_check.note: Move to the track-end car park/shelter.

unverified: Swimming and water-taxi pickup mentioned in the placement bio were not confirmed on a source page (OSM shows the public pier and ferry stop 'Anakiwa'); check before keeping 'swimming'.
Hours: open-access place, no published hours.

entries.name: Snout Walkway

facts.claim: Wikivoyage: peninsula between Picton and Waikawa Bay covered in native and exotic bush; tracks from a few minutes to 3.5 hours; free; Marlborough District Council map from the tourist information centre.

Marlborough NZ (regional tourism board): Snout Track begins at the Snout Track car park above Endeavour Park, goes to the Queen Charlotte View Lookout, then to a picnic area at the end of the headland; about 3 h return from the end car park, at least 4 h return from Picton.

Marlborough Online: begins in Victoria Domain above Picton, runs through regenerating coastal forest to the Snout lookout at the entrance to Waikawa Bay; mid-way clearing with picnic table; allow at least an hour each way.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Managed by Marlborough District Council; no council page was verified. marlboroughnz.com page (regional tourism board, title 'Snout Track | Marlborough NZ' verified) exists but is not an operator/steward site. Leave null unless the owner accepts the tourism board page.

coordinates_check.source: OSM tourism=viewpoint 'The Snout View' (-41.2506,174.0488), matches Wikivoyage
coordinates_check.note: This is the headland lookout at the far end, not the trailhead. Trailhead (Snout Track car park above Endeavour Park, Victoria Domain) could not be pinned from a structured source; candidate OSM points: Queen Charlotte View viewpoint (-41.2602,174.0353). Keep the headland point unless the owner wants the trailhead.

unverified: Exact trailhead/car park coordinates.

entries.name: Nydia Track

facts.claim: DOC: 27 km one way, advanced tramping track, 2-day tramp (or 5-8 hr mountain bike); climbs two saddles (Nydia 347 m, Kaiuma 387 m); overnight at Nydia Bay campsite (8 non-powered/tent sites).

Kaiuma Bay end: from Havelock turn off at Te Hoiere Road 2 km north, then Kaiuma Bay Road for 21 km to the track start on the roadside with a large sign. Duncan Bay end: road end and car park at Duncan Bay.
Charter launches and the mail boat run from Havelock to Shag Point, Nydia Bay or Duncan Bay.
Dogs only with a DOC permit; track passes through private land between Kaiuma and Nydia bays.

entries.cost_note: DOC page lists no track fee; the Nydia Bay campsite fee was not on the page (Nydia Lodge is private, bookings required). A Havelock water taxi/mail boat is optional and priced by operators (unverified).
entries.ticketUrl_note: DOC (managing agency) track page, loaded: title 'Nydia Track: Pelorus & Kenepuru Sounds area, Marlborough region'.

coordinates_check.source: OSM highway=path 'Nydia Track' southern start (-41.23477,173.79079) next to Kaiuma Bay Road, matching DOC 'Kaiuma Bay end'. Duncan Bay end car park: OSM amenity=parking (-41.11568,173.76515).
coordinates_check.note: Move to the Kaiuma Bay trailhead (reached by road from Havelock); the current point is mid-track.

entries.name: Wairau Lagoons

facts.claim: DOC: flat loop track (about 3 hr, easy to intermediate) along the lagoon shoreline with good bird watching to the rusting remains of the ship Waverley; no dogs.
Main access is from the end of Hardings Road, which leaves SH1 5 km south of Blenheim; there is a car park and information.
The lagoons formed over the last 6,500 years behind an 8 km boulder bank.

unverified: DOC gives no opening hours; 'Open 24 hours' is open-access assumption.

entries.name: Whites Bay

facts.claim: DOC Whites Bay campsite: 30 non-powered/tent sites close to a surf beach at Pukatea/Whites Bay; walking, fishing, swimming or kayaking; no dogs; no vehicles on the beach.
Campsite fees: adult $15, child (5-17) $7.50 per night, bookings required; gate closed 9 pm-7 am from Labour Weekend to Easter.
Whites Bay is 15 km from Tuamarina, off SH1 9 km north of Blenheim; alternative access is 41 km from Picton along the unsealed Port Underwood Road.
Rarangi-Whites Bay Track: 2.5 km one way, about 1 hr, between Whites Bay and Rarangi.

entries.hours_note: Beach is open access; the campsite gate is locked 9 pm-7 am from Labour Weekend to Easter.
entries.cost_note: Visiting the beach is free; only the campsite charges ($15 adult/night).
entries.ticketUrl_note: DOC (managing agency) Whites Bay campsite page, loaded: title 'Whites Bay conservation campsite: Blenheim area, Marlborough region'.

entries.name: Mount Richmond Forest Park

facts.claim: DOC: park between Nelson and Blenheim, 166,000 ha, the second largest forest park in New Zealand, gazetted 4 March 1977; the Richmond Range forms its backbone with peaks above 1700 m.

Northbank access from SH6 just north of the Wairau River Bridge (16 km from Blenheim); Top Valley has swimming holes, picnic and camping areas; Forks Walk is 4 km return (1 h 30) to Whiteheads Clearing, Riverside Walk 5 km return (2 h 30) past gold-mining remains.
Access roads cross forestry land and may be closed for forestry operations or fire danger.
Onamalutu Campsite: off SH6 west of Blenheim into Northbank Rd (~6 km), then Onamalutu Rd for 7 km; lat -41.45852, lon 173.70637.

entries.hours_note: Access roads can be closed by forestry operations and fire danger.
entries.cost_note: No park entry fee; campsites and huts are separate (Onamalutu $15 adult/night on the DOC page).
entries.ticketUrl_note: DOC (managing agency) park page, loaded: title 'Mount Richmond Forest Park: Places to go in Marlborough and Nelson/Tasman'.

coordinates_check.source: DOC Onamalutu Campsite page (Latitude -41.45852061, Longitude 173.70636536), the nearest DOC-listed access point to Blenheim on the Northbank side; the Top Valley Forks/Riverside carpark itself has no coordinates on DOC or in OSM
coordinates_check.note: Wikipedia point is a park centroid in the range. Onamalutu is a defensible Wairau-side visitor point; Mill Flat Campsite (-41.50110,173.51087, DOC) is the alternative deeper into the park. Owner to choose.

entries.name: Marfells Beach

facts.claim: DOC: Marfells Beach area: base at the campsite for water activities or follow the beach to Cape Campbell lighthouse; turn off SH1 onto Marfells Beach Rd 36 km south of Blenheim, then 8 km to the beach; no dogs.

Marfells Beach/Cape Campbell route: unmarked, expert route, about 4 hours along the beach; the second half to the lighthouse is low tide only; above the high tide line is private land; the lighthouse (second, built 1903) is at the southernmost extreme of Cook Strait.
Campsite: adult $15 per night, child (5-17) $7.50; campsite at lat -41.72548, lon 174.20446.

entries.cost_note: Beach is free; campsite charges $15 adult/night.

entries.name: Lake Grassmere

facts.claim: Wikivoyage: Lake Grassmere, where seawater is turned into huge piles of salt by the sun and evaporation; a birdwatcher's paradise; between Seddon and Ward on SH1.
Wikipedia: shallow lagoon 40 km south of Blenheim, used for salt production.
Earthcache page: the white salt piles are easily seen from SH1 at the end of summer.
Salt works operator is Dominion Salt (lake and refinery).

entries.hours_note: Roadside viewing only; the working salt works is not a public attraction (no visitor page found).

entries.name: Molesworth Station

facts.claim: DOC: Molesworth Recreation Reserve, 180,787 ha, New Zealand's largest farm, running the country's biggest beef herd (up to 10,000); Island Saddle (1347 m) is the highest point on a publicly accessed road in New Zealand.

Acheron Road is open 7 am-7 pm daily from 1 October to Easter Monday or the second Monday in April, whichever is later; it can close without warning; 207 km one way; caravans, buses or vehicles over 7 m are not permitted and a trailer needs a permit.

The 59 km section between Molesworth Cob Cottage and Acheron Accommodation House takes at least two hours; Cob Cottage (1866) is the gateway; Molesworth Homestead Lookout Track (10 min) starts behind the cottage.
Acheron Lookout Loop Walk: 1 km, 20 min, starts at Acheron Accommodation House; views of the house, Clarence River and valley.
Campsites: Cob Cottage (lat -42.08512, lon 173.27021) and Acheron Accommodation House (lat -42.39549, lon 172.95638), each $10 adult/night.

entries.hours_note: Acheron Road only, 1 Oct to Easter Monday / second Monday in April (whichever is later); closed to vehicles otherwise. Open now (today is 17 Oct 2026).
entries.cost_note: No driving fee or toll appears on any DOC Molesworth/Acheron page loaded (an unrelated search summary also found none); only campsites charge ($10 adult/night). Permits are needed for trailers and for use outside the open period.
entries.ticketUrl_note: DOC (managing agency) reserve page, loaded: title 'Molesworth Recreation Reserve: South Marlborough places to visit'. Alternative: https://www.doc.govt.nz/acheron-road (road status).

coordinates_check.source: DOC Molesworth Cob Cottage campsite page (Latitude -42.08511648, Longitude 173.27020624), DOC's 'gateway to Molesworth' on the Awatere (Blenheim) side
coordinates_check.note: Wikipedia point is a station centroid ~8 km west. Acheron Accommodation House alternative for the Hanmer side: -42.39549,172.95638.

unverified: Whether Molesworth is better described as 'Molesworth Recreation Reserve' (DOC's name); Wikipedia article title is 'Molesworth Station' (resolves).
Hours apply to the road; the reserve itself has no gate hours elsewhere.

entries.name: Rainbow Ski Area

facts.claim: Club-run ski area off SH63 near St Arnaud (1 h 20 from Blenheim, 1 h 40 from Picton); reached by a 12 km sealed Rainbow Valley Road with five fords, then an access road where carrying chains is mandatory.
2026 standard operating days are Saturdays and Sundays, with midweek days at the club's discretion.
Non-member lift day pass (all lifts) adult $130, student/senior $95, youth $75; learner lifts adult $85; season pass adult $390.
Non-skiers are asked for a suggested donation of $10 per adult and $5 per child.
Summer vehicle access to the lease area needs club membership and a $100 per-vehicle donation; foot and mountain bike access is permitted year-round without a permit.

entries.hours_note: Season dates are not fixed; the site banner at fetch time read 'Open Sunday 13/09 - No ski operations - visitor access only'. Operating days: Saturdays and Sundays.

entries.name: Ship Cove

facts.claim: Wikipedia 'Ship Cove' is a disambiguation page; the Marlborough Sounds article is titled 'Meretoto / Ship Cove' (the title 'Ship Cove, New Zealand' redirects to it).
DOC: Meretoto/Ship Cove was James Cook's favourite New Zealand base on his three voyages and is where the Queen Charlotte Track starts.

wiki_fix.note: Exact Wikipedia article title (spaces around the slash). Add `wiki: 'Meretoto / Ship Cove'` to the spot; the lead image is a view across the sound to Motuara Island from 2004, so check it against IMAGES.md before accepting.
